verdict.tagline: Seamless cooperative adventure built entirely for playing together.
for_you_if: you want a purely cooperative game built for two players
you enjoy shared split screen puzzle solving
you appreciate having a friend pass included
not_for_you_if: you prefer playing solo without a partner
you expect profound and serious writing
you lack a dedicated co op companion

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early players praise the generous friend pass and forgiving difficulty, though some find the dialogue bland.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that only one player needs to purchase the game because the second player can join using a friend's pass feature.

citations.review_text:
This was so much fun! The visuals are great, the story was sweet and more relevant than ever, the gameplay varied. Sometimes the checkpointing was a little wonky and some sections worked split-screen-wise better than others, but overall a must play for co-op-game lovers.
It's also worth noting that even when playing online, only one person actually needs to own the game for both to play, which is really apprechiated.

Exquisite!

I imagine that this story scratches an itch for many. Nothing majorly shocking. The story premise is not unique. HOWEVER, the way it flows and the design on which they tell it is unique! It really brings new life to old concepts. 

Ultra positive - the friend pass, no need for two people to buy it. 

Considerations: 

If you are someone who loves ultra complex games, this might not be for you. This game is designed to play like a friendlier Portal game with puzzles and a gameplay that plays like a movie. It is suited for all ages.  

All in all - 

My nickname for this game is "The Unintentional Betrayal" as you will likely kill your friend by hilarious accident frequently. And I wouldn't change a thing about this game!

[h1] Breathtaking Experience [/h1]

Got to know this amazing game from 2 streamers. When I bought it, the game was on a 50% discount(estimation). I can't lie, this game is absolutely amazing and in my opinion is quite a steal for it's original price. 

The friend's pass feature is such an amazing addition to the co-op experience especially with unemployed friends who refuse to spend money. Before using it, I was slightly worried this feature would require a list of confusing steps, but it was so simple anyone new to steam could do it without any help. 

I can't even say anything negative about this game, in all honesty. I crashed 2-3 times, which is fair given the fact that my laptop is a work-focused laptop and I'm in a discord call with my friends. If you have a similar laptop, prepare to have your fps at around 20-40(estimation) in most scenarios.

I would recommend this game to people who are willing to spend money on games and have close friends with free time. I'm planning to start another run with another friend since I just obtained my first completion and wanted to express how satisfied I was with my experience of this game. 

Would definitely recommend!
Very good. Only needed to buy one and able to play with my partner. Highly recommend for a 2-player coop game.

One of the most creative coop experiences I've ever played.  Excellent level design, epic action scenes, puzzles are simple but very creative, sound design is fantastic, and the story behind the playable characters have a satisfying payoff.  Highly recommended!  Only one person needs to buy the game, the second player gets to play for free with the friend's pass.
amazing story and visuals and big W for the friends pass

Really fun game. A lot of creative game mechanics. This is definitely a must buy for two people looking to play a fun co-op game. Only one person needs to purchase the game which is a plus. Graphics look great and game runs great. The story is the weak point for this game, doesn't compare to It Takes Two or A Way Out. Overall a great experience and I hope they continue to make games like these.

what a beautifully crafted game. amazing, yet trippy graphics and game mechanics. SO very good and worth the money. side note: it does have the "invite a friend to play" so someone can play with you if they don't have it.

Audio 10/10
graphics 10/10
gameplay 10/10
feelers getting soft 10/10
besties 10/10

They were robbed on the awards... this is one of the most innovative, surprising and fun games I've played in probably 2 decades.  An absolute bargain, especially when you can friend pass it with somebody on a different platform.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the platforming and gameplay as forgiving and not overly difficult for players who are less experienced.

citations.review_text:
After crushing it with It Takes Two, Hazelight absolutely hits another home run with Split Fiction. Same chill difficulty, top tier visuals n that cozy feel-good story vibe the studio’s famous for. What really blew me away most is the sidestory content. Every single arc’s got its own unique flavor n packed full of wild creativity, especially the hand-drawn storybook chapters. The level of polish there is straight up mind blowing.
Hope the devs keep this high quality streak going n drop more great games down the line.

it is beautiful and very thought-out, I love all the worlds, the story, the gameplay, everything. It is also very forgiving so it isn't too frustrating when you get things wrong or mess up. You can concentrate on the bonding experience rather than doing things right or wrong.

Split Fiction offers a story that will make you jump through time and space and alternate between stories set in Fantasy and in Sci-Fi. The gameplay is in the same vein as Hazelight Studios previous work, It Takes Two. I played this game with my partner who doesn’t really play video games and although some sections were difficult for them, we were able to finish the game together and had a lot of fun doing it. If you’re looking for a coop game with couch coop to play with a friend or partner that aren’t gamers, Split Fiction is a nice entry point.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the dialogue and writing as corny, cringe, or bland.

citations.review_text:
This was an absolute waste of my time. I will never get these 14 and a half hours back.

The premise was very interesting, but I imagined it a little different in terms of gameplay. I thought we'd actually have the different genres and worlds merge, which did not happen until the very end of the game, instead of just switching which one we're in together. At that point I already wanted to stop playing entirely.

The most irritating part was really just how painfully bad the writing is. The dialogue is extremely corny and unrealistic, and the characters' dynamics are pushed onto you without even having any actual substance. It starts off with them just constantly bickering, putting each other down, and being ridiculously negative all the time. They don't like each other's stories simply because they're different genres and have different plot points or visuals, so they just opt for insulting everything they don't like as if their opinions are the truth. It is genuinely the most pretentious piece of writing I have seen in a while.

Eventually the two main characters seem to form a bond, but at that point you just hate them both already anyway because they're pessimistic little ♥♥♥♥♥ with no appreciation for other people and their differences in taste. There is no reason for them to suddenly like each other. Everything about their dynamic comes off as purely obnoxious, unrealistic, and inherently boring. I have zero interest in either of these two or their stories, but the game still keeps shoving their little sob stories down your throat. They don't do anything to pull you in, yet still expect emotional investment.

Not to mention how much this game just keeps telling you everything straight up and treating the audience like a moron who cannot connect the dots themself. Every metaphor is just explained to you instead of letting you use your own brain to think about it and interpret it individually. Not that there was even much to interpret uniquely to begin with thoug…

Split Fiction looks stunning and plays well enough, but man, the writing is brutal. I went in hoping for something on par with A Way Out or It Takes Two, but narrative-wise, this is easily Hazelight's weakest game.

The execution is pure cringe. The dialogue is packed with "quirky" one-liners and forced banter that tries way too hard to be funny. It feels like millennial humour doing its absolute best to be funny and just missing every time. My co-op partner and I spent half the game just staring at each other in disbelief at what the characters were saying.

Story-wise, it's cliché after cliché. Nothing surprised me, nothing made me want to know what happened next, and I honestly never ended up caring what either character had to say. The plot itself is thin and predictable. I checked out around the halfway point and was basically just pushing through for the gameplay at that point.

Which is the frustrating part, because the game itself is actually solid. Visually it's incredible, and the co-op mechanics are fun more often than not. But these games live or die on their story, and this one just falls flat. Great graphics and fun co-op ideas can't carry writing this cheesy.

Grab it if you just want a decent co-op platformer, but set your expectations low if you've played any of Hazelight's other games.
Terrible writing and dialogue; way too much of it.

Very uninspired and very boring. The dialogue is cringy in some areas but it's mostly okay. The problem is that the game does very little to encourage teamwork. For 95% of the game you're just running down a hallway side by side and sometimes opening a door for the other before immediately rejoining. You may as well be playing a single player with how little interactivity that game has. The final level is creative and fun and is like what I expected the majority of the game, but it's only the final level. Pretty disappointing overall. Visually pretty but gameplay is a huge step-down from It Takes Two. There's also no puzzle solving or really anything to slow you down or work together. The powers you get each level are also incredibly boring and uncreative. Not the worst game but definitely not the best. We just didn't really have any fun playing it, like, at all. It's a shame.

Split fiction is honestly the most overrated game I have ever played and I’m shocked it’s overwhelming positive on steam.

I loved It Takes Two and A Way Out so it was such a shock to me that this game was a drag to get through, I was so hyped to play it when it got announced. However the writing, uninspired levels and characters just made this soo bleh.

The writing is the worse thing about this game, so if you’re looking for just a game for 2 player coop gameplay and don’t care about story at all, then this may be for you, but considering there’s so many other great choices with good writing this one falls flat. The dialogue in this game is just horrid as the main characters constantly shout out one outliers and when they’re not doing that you have to push through an obnoxiously optimistic character and a cringy edgy character. Throughout the entire game my friend and I were just groaning to the cringy dialogue and forced “you can talk to me, I’m here for you” moments, which sucks because I was really trying to get into the story, it’s just so painfully meh.

Not to mention the story is just boring / very obvious, you know how the story will end because the villain is very 1 dimensional. I did like how they tried to put a semi serious story segment near the end, but honestly I couldn’t care less by that point.

The idea of the game is cool, I like the sci-fi mix with fantasy, and honestly they have a really cool final level that mixes the two well, but most of the games levels are really boring and generic fantasy and sci-fi settings. The side stories are really cool however, they feel really creative and it feels like there’s passion put into them, it just sucks that they’re so small and the main levels are boring / very generic.

Another positive is the gameplay is mostly fun, if not repetitive. It feels like they just kinda took the gameplay of it takes two and redid it, which is not a bad thing I guess, just gets a bit repetitive.

Overall this game is just a …

The villain is so horrendously cliche and every line of dialogue feels like a first draft. Really disapointed because I enjoyed It Takes Two, and I LOVED A Way Out. It's ironic a story about writers is so poorly written. It's very unclear if these are novel authors, screenplay writers, or game writers? They just keep saying "writer" over and over again and refer to their work as "stories" instead of saying "book" or "film script". It sounds very unnatural. I wish there was more diversity in the sci-fi worlds. Most of them are just space, but sci-fi can be so much more than that! Like how Manware is more grounded on earth but everyone has robotic limbs and the technology is more advanced. The villain is just a super flat evil tech CEO. I wish he was at least funny or had SOME kind of interesting personality. I will say the gameplay can be fun at some parts, but the puzzles are so overly simple. It feels more like the game is a shallow rollercoaster ride than a good narrative or fun in depth game. This just feels like a step down from the studio's previous games.
One of if not the most creative game I have ever played. Only thing that hold it back is the bland dialog.

claims.claim: The game includes a Friend's Pass feature that allows a second player to join without purchasing a separate copy.

citations.review_text:
The story is so rich, the gameplay is engaging and at times a little bit tough! I would even say the game is underpriced since the friend pass exists. But to be honest the memories you're gonna make and laughs you're gonna have are what makes it worth it.

I got to experience all of this with my fav gamer on the planet, Aly. My first ever split screen game. I will forever chase the high of it.

Split Fiction
10 / 10

I am playing through this right now and it is an absolute blast. Josef Fares did it again. If you loved It Takes Two, this is literally that but on crack. It is the perfect game to play with your partner.

The Good
Zero repetition. The second you get used to a mechanic, the game takes it away and hands you something completely different. One minute you're wall-running in a cyberpunk city, the next you're riding a giant, colorful pig.
The Friend's Pass is a lifesaver. Only one of us had to buy it, and we are playing the whole thing together.
It looks absolutely stunning in 4K. No lag or frame drops even with a million things happening on a split screen.
The mid-boss checkpoints mean you won't break your controllers or argue over a hard fight.


The Bad

The villain is basically a cartoon CEO who is evil just for the sake of being evil. The story is a bit cheesy, but honestly, you're here for the gameplay anyway.

Buy it. Grab your partner. Lock yourself in a room for the weekend.

Game was absolutely amazing. Played It Takes Two with the gf, we loved it. bought this game, loved it as well. the game would stutter hard in a few spots, but looked absolutely stunning. Played through it a second time a few months later with a friend, his pc didnt stutter like mine did at times, he has a less powerful cpu, more powerful gpu, and windows 10 instead of 11. The game crashed twice wile playing with him, but was fine on his end, so i am chalking it up to windows 11 being not a good os. Share play (?) is an amazing feature as he had to download the game and not purchase it, and he loved it so much he left a very positive review. The story is great, fights are just the right difficulty where it would take some time with an inexperienced player, but some of them still took a few tries playing with an experienced one. Total hours currently wasted on secret level: 2

Highly recommed this game! 
First I played, It takes two then, A Way Out and lastly this, Split Fiction. 
Absolutely worth having all the three games to play with someone you know that has a galaxy wide of patience! 

Played all 3 games twice. Using friend's pass on the first playthrough. Bought all the games during sale time, bcoz I wanted to play it again but with a mission to get all the achievements. And so happy that I am able to, of course with the help of friends that has patience. 

I find it more fun and challenging doing the hunting achievements on this one, esp the [spoiler] Cold Potato and You Are Not A Robot (the capcha literally killed me) [/spoiler] . 

The shifting process between sci-fi and fantasy for me is so beautiful, like sci-fi are more into fast paced one, and its quite tricky to which is which to go next. While on fantasy is soothing and more of chillax one except for the [spoiler] flying kite one, thats so difficult like for real, real [/spoiler]
So its like, "ahh the stress of sci-fi is done for now, fantasy, here we go, yay! " 


Playing it again and recalling be like, "we did this on our first playthrough? I totally forgot." 🤣🤣🤣🤣

We was like, paused and look at the guide then continue again. Then laugh and have fun. 

Dont forget to always have fun while playing. Failing is the learning process. But in all honesty, I still have rusty reflexes on hands. 😂😂😂😂

Enjoy the game!

claims.claim: The levels alternate between sci-fi and fantasy themes associated with the two main characters.

citations.review_text:
A mi en lo personal me encantan los juegos de fantasía y ciencia ficción, así que la combinación de ambos para mi gusto fue increíble, sobretodo los escenarios y paisajes para cada parte de la historia son maravillosos. 
Cada historia, cada subtrama, tiene sus propias mecánicas, pero lo que llamó mi atención y me gustó muchísimo es que hagan guiños a otros juegos. 
La jugabilidad es bastante sencilla y fácil, me hubiese gustado que exista algo más de dificultad.
En cuanto a la historia y personajes principales pues siento que estuvo un poco flojo y bastante predecible. Y por último si tuviese que comparar la experiencia de Split Fiction con It Takes Two, diría que esta un pelin por debajo.

[h1]Missing the split-screen experience on a couch with a friend, partner or family member? Or simply just want to hop on to a nice co-op game? Then getting [b]Split Fiction[/b] is a total no-brainer![/h1]

I've finished the game three times with three different close friends, and I absolutely love it from start to finish. The amount of creativity developers put in this game is top notch. Love all the details and some references from many other games and even shows. Story writing was good, it starts off pretty slow and can be somewhat chaotic in the beginning. Game completion including side stories should take around 10-15 hours to beat. One of the character seems unlikeable due to her mean attitude, though as the story progresses her character develops near end, as well as to the part where they have to obtain the other fragment and lift each other's spirit up, I find this particular moment really beautiful.. I almost teared up. Both sci-fi and fantasy world designs are very well-made and gorgeous, sometimes ya just gotta halt for a while and just enjoy the scenery. Gameplay is packed with loads of actions especially in sci-fi world, the fantasy world on the other hand is much more chill. While the game isn't incredibly difficult but it definitely requires significant teamwork at times, hence proper communication is key. There are also two minigames available as side story which lets players to compete each other for fun. The music playing in the background is nicely composed too.

Overall the game is absolutely a blast to play, best part is the second player doesn't need to pay to experience the game! Will return to this game again for 100% achievements some other time when able. Definitely worth the full asking price, or at least try get it on sale if can. Much recommended for anyone who wants to have a fun co-op session with a friend/etc, you'll not be disappointed!

This game was INSANE. Easily one of the best co-op games I've played. The graphics are beautiful, the gameplay constantly changes, and the story just gets crazier the further you go.

I played as Mio while my duo played Zoe, and I loved how different their sci-fi and fantasy worlds felt. The ending was probably my favorite part. [spoiler] We were both playing in completely different-looking worlds while interacting with the same things, except everything appeared differently on each side. It was so trippy and such a cool way to end the game. [/spoiler]

Also loved seeing [spoiler] Cody and May at the Moon Market. 🥹 [/spoiler]

You will laugh, fight, yell at each other, get confused, and somehow still work together. Basically the complete duo experience. 😂

10/10. Beautiful, creative, chaotic, and absolutely worth playing with your duo.

claims.claim: The game features split-screen co-op where both players can see each other's perspectives.

citations.review_text: An excellent follow up to the series of incredible 2-player games after A Way Out and It Takes Two. Split Fiction (It Takes Three) blew us away with stunning graphics and innovative gameplay yet again. Without spoilers, the final segment of the game uses the split-screen border as a mechanic to act as an incredible gameplay, visual, and storytelling tool never seen before in gaming. Pick this game up with a mate for a peak bonding experience.

This game was INSANE. Easily one of the best co-op games I've played. The graphics are beautiful, the gameplay constantly changes, and the story just gets crazier the further you go.

I played as Mio while my duo played Zoe, and I loved how different their sci-fi and fantasy worlds felt. The ending was probably my favorite part. [spoiler] We were both playing in completely different-looking worlds while interacting with the same things, except everything appeared differently on each side. It was so trippy and such a cool way to end the game. [/spoiler]

Also loved seeing [spoiler] Cody and May at the Moon Market. 🥹 [/spoiler]

You will laugh, fight, yell at each other, get confused, and somehow still work together. Basically the complete duo experience. 😂

10/10. Beautiful, creative, chaotic, and absolutely worth playing with your duo.

This was honestly one of the best co-op games I have ever played. Playing this alongside my husband was such a wonderful experience. Wonderful gameplay for sci-fi and fantasy. You get the best of both worlds! I will definitely be coming back to this and playing as the other girl (Mio or Zoe) depending on who you start off as. The story itself is written beautifully and some of them will definitely make you super emotional. 
I also love the fact that Split Fiction is in fact split-screen. It's wonderful that you can see each other's  perspectives as you both progress throughout the game. I strongly recommend this game to everyone if you like RPG and action-based games. It is worth the money. It was extraordinary. 

*Side note... don't play if you get motion sick easily. It is very fast moving and split-screen.

I've completed it twice already, and honestly, I had an amazing time on both playthroughs. I think Hazelight has truly perfected its co-op formula. especially the way split screen gameplay becomes more than just a mechanic and actually feels like part of the story itself. That level of integration is genuinely impressive. Both it takes two and Split Fiction felt incredibly original to me. I couldn't say one is better than the other because each has its own charm, but Split Fiction definitely made me laugh a lot more. It's an excellent game to play with either a partner or friends. While it's relatively short, every moment feels worthwhile, and it's absolutely worth every penny:

The game is beyond my expectations. It gives you many vibes and excitement. Story is richer than I thought. Must try. Best with close friends. Lots of communications needed.

I had a blast playing this with my wife.  She's not a seasoned gamer so many of the various modes and perspectives they introduce really threw her, but it was simple enough that we managed to 100% everything in 25 hours.

Be ready to die many times, though checkpoints are very very plentiful which makes death just a nuisance.

You better be able to communicate and handle conflict with your partner, especially when you get to some of the more complicated bosses (I'm looking at you Robo-Mio) or that damn paddling section.  We never got too steamed at each other but it can be pretty stressful.

That said, the funniest parts were exactly those moments where you shared control somehow.  Centipede acrobatics... is something I never thought I would write... and also one of the best parts.

If you can find someone who will endure arguing with you for 20+ hours, or who is legally obligated to do so, this one is definitely worthy of a playthrough.
Very unique, fun co-op gameplay. The levels aren't too difficult but do require good communication.
